title: Walter Sorrells on Japanese Bladesmithing, Martial Arts, and the Artisan's Journey

sentences.en: But welcome to the Taproot Therapy Collective's podcast, Discover, Hear, Grow.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 Taproot Therapy Collective 的播客“探索、倾听、成长”。

sentences.en: I'm here with Walter Sorrells, who's a sword and knife maker, forge master in Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人，今天请到了沃尔特·索雷尔斯（Walter Sorrells），他是亚特兰大的刀剑制作者、锻造大师。

sentences.en: And we're excited to get into learning about some of his art.
sentences.zh: 我们很高兴能来了解一些他的艺术创作。

sentences.en: We tried to connect for a while, but I finally tracked you down and one of us will die with honor today.
sentences.zh: 我们联系了一段时间，我终于找到你了，今天我们俩必须有一个人带着荣誉死去。

sentences.en: So I've heard that you are a good teacher.
sentences.zh: 所以我听说你是一位好老师。

sentences.en: I would like a lesson.
sentences.zh: 我想上一课。

sentences.en: Is what I have heard you're supposed to say when you go into the opposing dojo and you're challenging the, you know, master of the.
sentences.zh: 这就是传说中你走进对方道场，去向那个，你知道的，大师挑衅时应该说的话吗。

sentences.en: So can you tell us a little bit about your work?
sentences.zh: 那么你能跟我们聊聊你的工作吗？

sentences.en: You're in Atlanta and you're a blacksmith and you, I don't want to say forger because then it's maybe the IRS will come after you.
sentences.zh: 你在亚特兰大是一名铁匠，你，我不想说你是造假者，不然税务局可能会找上门。

sentences.en: But what do you, how do you call your, what do you call yourself?
sentences.zh: 但你，你怎么称呼你的，你自称什么？

sentences.en: Do you still go by blacksmith or?
sentences.zh: 你现在还自称铁匠吗？

sentences.en: Uh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 呃，对。

sentences.en: I mean, honestly, I do a lot less blacksmithing than I used to.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，说实话，我现在做的铁匠活比以前少多了。

sentences.en: Um, you know, when I got started, I was making Japanese swords pretty much exclusively.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，我刚开始的时候，几乎只做日本刀。

sentences.en: And, um, you know, just over time, I kind of evolved into making more modern, uh, knives and kind of production, um, type knives, semi-production knives.
sentences.zh: 然后，嗯，随着时间推移，我逐渐开始制作更多现代的、嗯，刀具以及那种量产型的、嗯，半量产型的刀具。

sentences.en: Um, and actually these days I'm making a lot of tools.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实现在我在做很多工具。

sentences.en: I make tools for, uh, Japanese sword making, um, and, uh, you know, just general knife making.
sentences.zh: 我为制作日本刀，嗯，还有，你知道的，一般的制刀业制作工具。

sentences.en: Um, so, yeah, I've seen your work and that was what led me to reach out and then I couldn't believe you're so close.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，是的，我见过你的作品，这也是我联系你的原因，然后我简直不敢相信你离得这么近。

sentences.en: Um, the, the, uh, I think I saw like a, a Japanese sword that had a burl sire, which is, I mean, carving burl is hard enough.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那个，那个，嗯，我好像看到了一把日本刀，它的刀柄是树瘤木的，我的意思是，雕刻树瘤木已经够难的了。

sentences.en: I can't imagine, um, having to, to be able to keep it, you know, pretty and also, um, you get it right.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象，嗯，还要保证它，你知道的，既漂亮，而且，嗯，还要做对。

sentences.en: So, I mean, you're quite a craftsman.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，你真是一位了不起的工匠。

sentences.en: Um, are most of those pieces kind of commission or you, you know, make a lot and take them to specialty markets or how does, how does that work?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些作品大多是定制的吗，还是说，你知道的，你做好多然后拿到专业市场去卖，或者说这到底是怎样的流程？

sentences.en: So when I got started, uh, it was all commission, you know, Japanese sword stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以我刚开始做的时候，嗯，全都是定制的，你知道，都是日本刀之类的东西。

sentences.en: So people would say, I want a sword yay long and, you know, specify all kinds of stuff about it.
sentences.zh: 所以人们会说，我想要一把这么长的刀，然后，你知道，对它提出各种具体要求。

sentences.en: Um, and that is just a giant pain in the neck.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那简直是个让人头疼的大麻烦。

sentences.en: So, um, over time I've kind of evolved away from doing custom work.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，随着时间推移，我逐渐不再接定制工作了。

sentences.en: Um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: you know, it's one of those things that you learn a lot from doing custom work, but at the same time, it's just very, if, if this is your income, if you're doing it for fun,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是那种通过做定制能学到很多东西的事情，但与此同时，如果这是你的收入来源，如果你只是为了好玩，那就是另一回事了。

sentences.en: it's one thing.
sentences.zh: 那是一回事。

sentences.en: But if you're, if it's your income source, you're always dependent on whether somebody likes it, whether it was the thing, you know, I mean,
sentences.zh: 但如果你，如果这是你的收入来源，你总是得看别人是不是喜欢，是不是他们想要的东西，你知道，我的意思是，

sentences.en: there are a lot of people who buy stuff.
sentences.zh: 有很多人买东西。

sentences.en: Just generally.
sentences.zh: 通常来说。

sentences.en: And they feel like if I just buy this thing, my life is going to be so much better.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得只要我买了这东西，我的生活就会变得好得多。

sentences.en: And especially people who kind of nerd out on a particular sort of thing, and they're spending a bunch of money on it and all that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 尤其是那些对某类特定事物有点痴迷的人，他们在这上面花了一大笔钱之类的。

sentences.en: They have all these expectations and you just never know.
sentences.zh: 他们抱有各种各样的期望，而你永远猜不到结果。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's a train wreck, you know, and it's some, it's usually not anything you did.
sentences.zh: 有时这会是一场灾难，你知道，而且通常这并不是因为你做了什么，

sentences.en: It's just that, you know, they had expectations that don't align with whatever you actually produced.
sentences.zh: 只是因为，你知道，他们的期望跟你实际做出来的东西并不一致。

sentences.en: And, um,
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，

sentences.en: You get people that want custom art, but they don't trust the artists to, you know, kind of put themselves into something or the, you know,
sentences.zh: 你会遇到想要定制艺术品的人，但他们又不信任艺术家，不愿意让艺术家把自己的个性融入其中，或者，你知道，

sentences.en: That's, that's kind of true.
sentences.zh: 这倒也确实。

sentences.en: Um, and so, um, you know, the, the, the perfect kind of client for me is somebody who says, I want it, you know, a 26 inch long blade with such and such geometry.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，嗯，你知道，对我来说最完美的客户是那种会说“我想要一把26英寸长的刀刃，要某种特定的几何形状”的人。

sentences.en: You go and just do it however you want.
sentences.zh: “你去吧，随你怎么做都行。”

sentences.en: And those guys are a joy to work for.
sentences.zh: 跟这种人合作简直是一种享受。

sentences.en: Uh, and there, that's about half the, half the customers and the other set are crazy people and they're very hard to work with.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且这种客户大概占了一半，另一半则是疯子，他们非常难合作。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I can imagine it would be like, um, what is it?
sentences.zh: 我可以想象，那会是怎样的，嗯，怎么说呢？

sentences.en: One of my friends, Todd Johnson does these like custom pipes, but they're like, you know, hundreds of, uh, where they're like, you know, some of them will be like pushing $10,000,
sentences.zh: 我的一个朋友托德·约翰逊（Todd Johnson）制作这种定制烟斗，但它们的价格，你知道的，有几百个，或者说它们的价格，你知道，其中一些甚至会逼近10,000美元，

sentences.en: you know, for a pipe.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就为了一个烟斗。

sentences.en: Cause they're more like art pieces.
sentences.zh: 因为它们更像是艺术品。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he was talking about the presentation of it that a lot of people go in and they're like great carpenters, but, um, they talk about the pipes that they make or something.
sentences.zh: 他谈到过这种展示方式，很多人入行时都是优秀的木工，但是，嗯，他们谈论自己制作的烟斗或者别的什么时，

sentences.en: And he was just like, you know, I had the language of fine arts and I went into this and I talk about pieces that I place in a collection.
sentences.zh: 他当时就觉得，你知道，我掌握了纯艺术的语言，我进入了这个领域，我谈论的是我放入收藏馆的作品。

sentences.en: And that, you know, a lot of that is kind of the, the difference where you just kind of tell the market what you are.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这其中很大一部分区别就在于，你得告诉市场你是什么定位。

sentences.en: And in a certain way, you tell the market to screw off, you know, certain segments,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，你甚至得对市场说“去你的”，你知道，针对某些细分市场，

sentences.en: but I want Buffalo horn on it and I want it to look like an anime and I want it to be able to,
sentences.zh: “但我想要水牛角做的，我想要它看起来像动漫里的那样，我还想要它能够，”

sentences.en: you know, right.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对吧。

sentences.en: Well, and, and you do learn after a certain point to say no.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，在经历过某些事情之后，你确实会学会说“不”。

sentences.en: Um, but you know, when I first got started, I mean, there were sort of two, two factors that coincided to get me into some trouble at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不过你知道，我刚开始的时候，也就是说，当时有大约两个因素同时起作用，让我一开始惹上了一些麻烦。

sentences.en: Uh, the first was really just not knowing what I was doing.
sentences.zh: 第一，其实就是不知道自己在干什么。

sentences.en: I mean, from a commercial perspective, I I've been a writer for a long, long time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从商业角度来看，我当了很长时间很长时间的作家。

sentences.en: That was really my real profession until I got, uh, I was a noveliSt.
sentences.zh: 在我转行之前，那确实是我的真正职业，我是一名小说家。

sentences.en: So I wrote mystery novels.
sentences.zh: 所以我写悬疑小说。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 酷。

sentences.en: Like, uh, like kind of film noir, hard boiled or more true crime or what, what was, uh, I mean, I've, I've written everything.
sentences.zh: 像，呃，像黑色电影那种冷硬派风格，还是更偏向真实犯罪，或者说，到底是什么样的，我的意思是，我写过各种各样的东西。

sentences.en: Uh, I, I started doing legal thrillers.
sentences.zh: 呃，我一开始写的是法律惊悚小说。

sentences.en: Uh, this would have been back around 1990, I guess.
sentences.zh: 呃，这大概是在1990年前后吧。

sentences.en: No, is that?
sentences.zh: 不对，是那样吗？

sentences.en: Well, anyway, whenever it was, it was a long, long time ago.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，反正那是很久很久以前的事了。

sentences.en: And, um, I sort of evolved out of that and I had different pseudonyms and I wrote, uh, I wrote, uh, my ghost wrote things.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，我慢慢不再写那种了，我有过不同的笔名，我写过，呃，我写过代笔的东西。

sentences.en: And I wrote, I mean, just endless stuff.
sentences.zh: 我写过，我的意思是，各种无穷无尽的东西。

sentences.en: Um, I mean, and this sort of dovetails with the second part of the, of the issue for me.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，这正好和我的第二个问题吻合。

sentences.en: The first was, I, I, I didn't really know how long it would take to make some of these swords and things like that.
sentences.zh: 第一个是，我，我，我真的不知道制作这些剑之类的东西到底需要多长时间。

sentences.en: And so I, I kind of committed myself to myself to some things that were, um, you know, that I underpriced and,
sentences.zh: 所以，我，我给自己承接了一些，嗯，你知道的，我定价过低的项目，

sentences.en: and I just didn't realize how long it was going to take to deliver them.
sentences.zh: 而且我根本没意识到交付它们需要花这么长时间。

sentences.en: Um, um, the other thing though, was, uh, you know, when I got started doing this, um, I was just in a financially precarious position and I just needed the money.
sentences.zh: 嗯，嗯，不过另一件事是，嗯，你知道，当我刚开始做这个的时候，嗯，我的财务状况非常不稳定，我太需要钱了。

sentences.en: And so I said yes to some things that, you know, in retrospect, um, you know, were a mistake, but.
sentences.zh: 所以我答应了一些，你知道，现在回想起来，嗯，你知道，是个错误的事情，但是。

sentences.en: What got you into Japanese swords and katanas the way that, I mean, cause there's a lot to that process.
sentences.zh: 是什么让你迷上日本刀和武士刀的？因为我的意思是，这个过程有很多门道。

sentences.en: It's not like, uh, usually that's not what people start with, you know, um, well, uh, you know, I was, uh, I was a Japanese, uh, uh, martial arts nut for a long time.
sentences.zh: 这不像，呃，通常这不是人们一开始就会接触的东西，你知道，嗯，好吧，嗯，你知道，我，呃，我曾是一个日本，嗯，嗯，武术迷，持续了很长时间。

sentences.en: Um, I did, uh, karate for about 20 years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我练了大约20年空手道。

sentences.en: Uh, I did, um, a Japanese sword art called, uh, Shinkendo probably for, you know, a little under a decade.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我练过一种叫做，呃，神剑道（Shinkendo）的日本剑术，大概有，你知道，不到十年吧。

sentences.en: Um, and, you know, I did various other things, Brazilian jujitsu and stuff.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，我还练过其他各种各样的东西，比如巴西柔术之类的。

sentences.en: And, uh, so anyway, actually, um, I mean, specifically what happened was I was going to write this book that, uh, I was going to have a main character who was a swordsmith.
sentences.zh: 然后，不管怎样，其实，嗯，我的意思是，具体发生的事情是，我当时打算写一本书，嗯，书里有一个主角是一名刀匠。

sentences.en: And, you know, so I said, well, I mean, I always like as a writer to get my hands around stuff, you know, I want to go to the neighborhood where the thing happens.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，所以我说，好吧，我的意思是，作为一个作家，我总是喜欢亲自去接触各种事物，你知道，我想去事情发生的地方。

sentences.en: You know, I want to meet the guy who does the thing, you know?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想去见那个做这行的人，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And so, uh, in this particular case, I was like, well, let me just screw around a little bit and figure out how, you know, how it works physically.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，在这个特定的情况下，我想，好吧，让我稍微瞎折腾一下，弄清楚它是怎么，你知道的，在物理上是如何运作的。

sentences.en: Like what it feels like in your hand to do this stuff.
sentences.zh: 比如你手里拿着这东西是什么感觉。

sentences.en: And I really just farted around and, and I mean, I just, I got the bug like that.
sentences.zh: 我真的只是瞎胡闹了一通，而且，我的意思是，我一下子就着迷了。

sentences.en: It just, it just hit me like a hammer.
sentences.zh: 它就像锤子一样狠狠地砸中了我。

sentences.en: Uh, and, uh, you know, so I, I really went probably 15 years where in essence I was doing two full-time jobs.
sentences.zh: 呃，而且，你知道，所以我，我大概有15年的时间，实际上同时在做两份全职工作。

sentences.en: So, um, you know, I would write in the, at the beginning of the day and then I'd start, uh, doing, doing, uh, sword making in the afternoon.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，你知道，我会在一天刚开始的时候写作，然后下午开始，呃，开始做，做刀剑制作。

sentences.en: And sometimes that would run up until, you know, midnight or something.
sentences.zh: 有时甚至会一直干到，你知道，半夜左右。

sentences.en: And it was, it was, uh, it was just seven days a week of, of work.
sentences.zh: 而且，那真是，那是，呃，每周七天连轴转的工作。

sentences.en: And after a while, I finally was like, I just got to do one of these things.
sentences.zh: 过了一段时间，我终于觉得自己受够了，必须专注于其中一件事。

sentences.en: So, so I've been doing this full-time for a decade or so.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以我全职做这个已经有十年左右了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I haven't like written published fiction for a while, but I used to a little bit short form stuff.
sentences.zh: 我已经有一段时间没写出版的小说fiction了，但我以前写过一点短篇。

sentences.en: And I would notice that, that a lot of what I was trying to write about, I was kind of trying to chew on something and it ended up becoming, even though it's fiction,
sentences.zh: 我发现，我试图写的很多东西，我其实是在琢磨某些事情，最后它变成了一种，尽管它是虚构的，

sentences.en: like it ended up kind of becoming something that I was working on artistically or personally.
sentences.zh: 但它最终变成了一种我在艺术上或个人层面上正在解决的事情。

sentences.en: And the, you know, the, the characters that I was kind of being, what if a guy did this?
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，那些我一直在构思的角色，比如“如果一个人这么做了会怎样？”

sentences.en: And I would learn about that.
sentences.zh: 然后我会去了解这方面的情况。

sentences.en: So I know what I'm talking about, you know, end up being something that I just kind of wanted to do, but, you know, on some level it wasn't, um, didn't see myself as,
sentences.zh: 这样我就知道自己在说些什么了，你知道，最后它成了我内心某种想做的事，但从某种程度上说，并不是，呃，我没把自己看作那样的人，

sentences.en: but could see a character as.
sentences.zh: 而是把一个角色看作那样的人。

sentences.en: And then, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 然后，我不知道。

sentences.en: Can you say anything about that?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这方面的感受吗？

sentences.en: Or was that a similar thing?
sentences.zh: 还是说你也有过类似的情况？

sentences.en: Um, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道。

sentences.en: I, I, uh, you know, it really, it depended on the book that I was working on, honestly, because sometimes, um, you know, I would, I would be doing something on a deadline.
sentences.zh: 我，我，嗯，你知道，这真的取决于我当时正在写的那本书，说实话，因为有时，嗯，你知道，我会，我是在赶截稿日期写作。

sentences.en: And it was really just mash that stuff out and whatever it took to get it done was what it took.
sentences.zh: 那真的就是硬着头皮把东西赶出来，不管需要付出什么代价都要把它完成。

sentences.en: Um, and I, and honestly, when I first got started though, you don't love everything you have to write as a professional writer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，说实话，我刚开始的时候，作为一个专业作家，你其实并不喜欢你必须写的所有东西。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: No, no doubt.
sentences.zh: 没错，毫无疑问。

sentences.en: Um, even in some parts of the same book that you do like to write, you're not the part you want to write.
sentences.zh: 嗯，甚至在同一本书的某些部分里，虽然你喜欢写，但它并不是你最想写的那部分。

sentences.en: Right, right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对。

sentences.en: Um, but, uh, you know, I also, um, uh, when I first got started, I do a lot, a lot of research.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不过，嗯，你知道，我同时，呃，呃，我刚开始的时候，我做了大量大量的研究。

sentences.en: Um, I mean, I got a job selling cars one time for a, for a book that I was working on.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，为了我当时正在写的一本书，我曾经去应聘过一份卖汽车的工作。

sentences.en: Um, and, uh, you know, I did a lot of crime fiction.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，嗯，你知道，我写了很多犯罪小说。

sentences.en: So I was always interviewing district attorneys and cops and guys like that.
sentences.zh: 所以我总是在采访地区检察官、警察和诸如此类的人。

sentences.en: And, um, you know, so that stuff is always really useful, but sometimes it can lead you to, you know, oh, I learned all this cool stuff.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，你知道，所以这些素材总是非常有用，但有时它也会把你引入歧途，比如，哦，我学到了这么多酷炫的东西，

sentences.en: So let me jam it into the story.
sentences.zh: 让我把它硬塞进故事里吧。

sentences.en: So it's, it, sometimes you can overdo it.
sentences.zh: 所以，这，有时候你会用力过猛。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You can definitely spot, especially with like crime fiction, over-researched work where somebody's going on about DNA and apoptosis and electrophagesis gel.
sentences.zh: 你绝对能一眼看出那些过度查阅资料的作品，尤其是犯罪小说，里面有人喋喋不休地谈论DNA、细胞凋亡和凝胶电泳。

sentences.en: And it's like, well, I'm glad you think that's cool, but I don't know that we need to.
sentences.zh: 然后就会觉得，好吧，我很高兴你觉得这很酷，但我不知道我们是否有必要……

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: There's, um, when, when your work with martial arts, was that, was there anything that kind of helped you grow personally or, you know,
sentences.zh: 当你在练武术时，有没有什么东西在某种程度上帮助你在个人层面上成长，或者说，你知道的，

sentences.en: called you to it from like a history of you working through something?
sentences.zh: 是因为你过去一直在解决某些问题，才被它吸引过去的？

sentences.en: And then myself, um, I just started some, I'm a baby, um, still with the wooden sword, but, um, and then James weights at our practice, uh,
sentences.zh: 而我自己，嗯，我刚刚开始接触，我还太嫩，嗯，手里还拿着木刀，但是，嗯，然后我们训练时的詹姆斯（James）说，

sentences.en: we both do shikendo and I'd wanted to do like a, a historical martial arts.
sentences.zh: 我们两个都在练神剑道，而且我一直想练一种，历史上的武术。

sentences.en: It was actually effective for a long time.
sentences.zh: 一种在很长时间里真正有效的武术。

sentences.en: Like a lot of times with just kendo or fencing or some schools of stuff,
sentences.zh: 就像很多时候，通过剑道（kendo）或击剑或某些流派的东西，

sentences.en: they turn it more into a sport where you're kind of like doing things that wouldn't actually work if you were in a fight, but you know, you get a point for it or something.
sentences.zh: 他们把它变成了一种运动，你会去做一些在真正的战斗中其实根本不管用的动作，但你知道，你能因此得分或者别的什么。

sentences.en: And, and so I always wanted to do something that was like, you know, really effective and shikendo was, and I'm, was working through some things.
sentences.zh: 所以，我一直想学一些像这样，你知道的，真正有效的武术，神剑道就是这样，而且我当时正在克服一些问题。

sentences.en: I had kind of had a point where something happened and I realized like, I need to learn on to be more, more assertive.
sentences.zh: 我曾经历过一个时刻，发生了某件事，我意识到，我需要学会变得更加自信。

sentences.en: And I need to really deal with some of the stuff that I'm running away from.
sentences.zh: 我需要真正去面对我一直在逃避的一些事情。

sentences.en: Um, and, um, just things like as simple as like having to keep your weight forward, you know, it, it really like challenges my posture.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，就像一些非常简单的事情，比如必须保持身体重心向前，你知道，它，它真的对我的体态提出了挑战。

sentences.en: I feel all this stuff kind of come up from, from childhood where I don't, I don't feel like it's safe to be assertive.
sentences.zh: 我能感觉到所有这些情绪从童年时期涌上心头，那时候我觉得表现得自信并不安全。

sentences.en: And I mean, it psychologically is hard and draining, which is, you know, I want to do something hard that, that makes me grow at this point in my life,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在心理上这很难，也很消耗精力，这也就是，我想要在这个人生阶段做一些困难的、能让我成长的事，

sentences.en: which is kind of why I'm doing it.
sentences.zh: 这也是我为什么要练这个的原因。

sentences.en: Um, what was your relationship to kind of martial arts and stuff before you got into the, they brought you to the sword making?
sentences.zh: 嗯，在你接触武术并最终走上制刀之路前，你跟武术之类的东西有着怎样的渊源？

sentences.en: Well, you know, I think that a lot of, um, uh, a lot of martial arts people are, uh, you know, kind of nerds who are compensating, you know?
sentences.zh: 好吧，你知道，我觉得很多，嗯，呃，很多练武之人，呃，你知道，都是些想要找平衡的书呆子，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Guilty.
sentences.zh: 我承认。

sentences.en: You know, but, but also, I, um, my, uh, my sister's ex-husband who actually just died last night.
sentences.zh: 你知道，不过，不过还有，我，呃，我姐姐的前夫，他其实昨晚刚去世。

sentences.en: Um, well, yeah, it's a sad thing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，好吧，这真是一件令人难过的事。

sentences.en: Um, anyway, uh, he, um, once said to me, I'm a nerd athlete and I had this weird sense of recognition, like at age 40, I realized, oh yeah, you're exactly right, Joe.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不管怎样，呃，他，嗯，曾对我说过，“我是个书呆子运动员”，我当时有一种奇怪的共鸣感，就像在40岁时，我意识到，哦，是的，乔，你完全说对了，

sentences.en: I'm a nerd athlete too.
sentences.zh: 我也是个书呆子运动员。

sentences.en: I'd always loved athletics and was a, you know, pretty athletic person, but I never, you know, I never conceived myself as a jock.
sentences.zh: 我一直很喜欢运动，而且，你知道的，身体也算相当矫健，但我从来，你知道，我从不把自己看作是一个体育健将。

sentences.en: You know, I was always the, the nerdy brainy kind of guy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我一直都是那种书呆子、高智商型的家伙。

sentences.en: Um, and so, you know, I, I felt like, um, martial arts is a really natural avenue for people with that kind of psychology, I think.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，你知道，我觉得，嗯，对于拥有这种心理特征的人来说，武术真的是一条非常自然的途径。

sentences.en: Um, but beyond that, um, you know, I think everybody goes into martial arts and learn something different.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，嗯，你知道，我觉得每个人接触武术都会学到不同的东西。

sentences.en: I mean, I, you know, I've known people who said I was out of control and this helped me, you know, control my aggressions.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我，你知道的，我认识一些人，他们说我曾经无法控制自己，而这个帮我，你知道的，控制了我的攻击性。

sentences.en: I've known people who said I was too timid and this learned to make me more confident and aggressive.
sentences.zh: 我认识一些人，他们说我太怯懦，而这个让我学会了变得更加自信和具有攻击性。

sentences.en: Um, and so, you know, I think everybody has to find their path inside of a martial art and that's really part of your job as a martial artiSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，你知道的，我认为每个人都必须在武术中找到自己的道路，这确实是你作为武术家职责的一部分。

sentences.en: It's not just kicking and punching or whatever.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是踢腿、出拳什么的。

sentences.en: It's turning your eyes towards yourself and trying to figure out, okay, who is this guy that's doing this thing?
sentences.zh: 这是把你的目光转向内心，试着弄清楚，好吧，做这件事的这个家伙到底是谁？

sentences.en: And what will then make him more effective, you know, killing the opponent on the inside, you know,
sentences.zh: 然后是什么会让他更有效率，你知道的，从内部杀死对手，你知道的，

sentences.en: breaking the shadow and all that Jungian and Joseph Campbell stuff is definitely relevant.
sentences.zh: 打破阴影以及所有荣格和约瑟夫·坎贝尔的那一套理论绝对是相关的。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，绝对是。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对的。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, a Japanese sword is not an easy thing to jump into making.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，日本刀可不是那种说做就能轻易上手制作的东西。

sentences.en: I mean, you've got multiple types of metal, you've got clay tempering, you've got, you know, really specific tolerances.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你有多种金属类型，你有覆土淬火，你有，你知道的，非常严格的公差标准。

sentences.en: I mean, you can kind of bring out a European broadsword that's serviceable, but that's, that's a complicated thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你大概能弄出一把勉强能用的欧洲宽剑，但那个，那个是复杂的东西。

sentences.en: Can you say anything about kind of that process?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈那种工艺吗？

sentences.en: And, um, yeah, I mean, you know, I, I, I am, you know, I, part of my nerd quality is that I just love learning things and I'm very focused and very, you know,
sentences.zh: 还有，嗯，对，我的意思是，你知道，我，我，我，你知道，我，我的书呆子特质之一就是我只是热爱学习新事物，而且我非常专注，非常，你知道的，

sentences.en: when I dive into something, I really hit it hard.
sentences.zh: 当我投入到某件事中时，我真的是全力以赴。

sentences.en: And so I just immersed myself in it, of course, you know, I'd been using Japanese swords for a while and, you know, I had some concept of what this tool was supposed to do.
sentences.zh: 所以我就让自己沉浸其中，当然，你知道的，我用日本刀有一段时间了，你知道的，我对这个工具应该做什么有一些概念。

sentences.en: And that really, I think, helped me frame how I went about it.
sentences.zh: 而那真的，我认为，帮助我构建了我着手进行的方式。

sentences.en: And, and I, you know, maybe I, I, it's a little pretentious to say it, it, it, it increased the seriousness of what I was doing, but I did, I did want to, like,
sentences.zh: 而且，而且我，你知道，也许我，我，说这话有点自命不凡，它，它，它增加了我所做事情的严肃性，但我确实，我确实想要，就像，

sentences.en: there are a lot of people who make Japanese kind of styled, sharp, pointy things who don't really work too hard to get the historical details right.
sentences.zh: 有很多人制作日本风格的、锋利的、尖锐的东西，他们并没有真正努力把历史细节弄对。

sentences.en: And that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And that was something that was very interesting to me and very, it was important to me in terms of what I was trying to do.
sentences.zh: 而那是我非常感兴趣的事，而且对于我试图做的事情来说非常、非常重要。

sentences.en: And so, um, you know, I never went to Japan.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，你知道，我从未去过日本。

sentences.en: I was never apprenticed or anything like that, but I mean, I read every book in the English language about Japanese swords.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有当过学徒或类似的事情，但我的意思是，我读了英语世界里每一本关于日本刀的书。

sentences.en: I, you know, I, I talked to people, of course I did train to, and, and so, you know,
sentences.zh: 我，你知道，我，我和人们交谈过，当然我也确实进行过训练，所以，你知道，

sentences.en: I just kind of triangulated and tried to cram as much information as I could into that experience so that what I was making, you know, fit into my idea of this, this sword.
sentences.zh: 我只是进行了某种三角测量，并试图将尽可能多的信息塞进那段经历中，这样我制造的东西，你知道，就符合了我对这把，这把剑的想法。

sentences.en: Now I would also say, I was never trying to be like a Japanese sword maker, you know, I, everybody who's Tori Hanzo or something.
sentences.zh: 现在我也想说，我从来没想过要成为一个日本刀匠，你知道的，每个人都是服部半藏或者别的什么。

sentences.en: Right, right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, everybody who's in martial arts for a while will meet some people who try to become Japanese sort of, you know, they imagine themselves to become,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，每个练武术一段时间的人都会遇到一些人，他们试图变成某种日本的，你知道的，他们想象自己变成，

sentences.en: I was never into that.
sentences.zh: 我从来对那个不感兴趣。

sentences.en: And, and, and so I always felt, I mean, it's partly kind of an uncomfortable thing and in, and in probably in certain respects,
sentences.zh: 而且，而且，所以我一直觉得，我的意思是，这在某种程度上有点让人不舒服，而且在，而且可能在某些方面，

sentences.en: it's why I've stepped back a little bit from Japanese sword making, because I just felt like after a certain point, you know, there's a limit to where I can go with it.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我对制作日本刀稍微退缩了一点，因为我只是觉得在某个时期之后，你知道，我在这条路上能走多远是有限度的。

sentences.en: Um, but I always felt like, Hey, I'm a, an, an American guy making this stuff.
sentences.zh: 但是，我总是觉得，嘿，我是一个，一个，一个制造这些东西的美国人。

sentences.en: You know, I was never trying to project myself into some mythical Japanese world or something.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我从来没有试图把自己投射到一个神话般的日本世界或其他什么地方。

sentences.en: Um, and so, you know, basically I can get uncomfortable when you look at some,
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，你知道的，基本上当你看到一些，

sentences.en: some people like it gets uncomfortable the way they mythologize the self and like pretend they're part of some lineage where it's like, Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 一些人的时候，我会感到不舒服，他们神话自我并假装自己是某个血统的一部分，那种方式让人很不舒服，就像，哦，好吧。

sentences.en: You know?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，对，确实如此。

sentences.en: Um, so anyway, you know, I, I, I, I just, I just really immersed myself in it and tried to, you know, try to learn as much as I could.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以无论如何，你知道，我，我，我，我只是，我只是真正让自己沉浸其中，并试图，你知道，尽量学到尽可能多的东西。

sentences.en: And a lot of us just trial and error.
sentences.zh: 而且很多都是通过反复试验得来的。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think a lot of people, um, feel like they need to have somebody teach them to do X or Y or Z.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我认为很多人，嗯，觉得他们需要有人教他们做这样、那样或别的事。

sentences.en: And I've always been a little bit of an anti-authoritarian, do it myself guy to a fault, you know, and there are advantages to having that kind of character.
sentences.zh: 而我一直有点反权威，骨子里是个习惯自己动手的独行侠，你知道的，拥有这种性格有它的优势。

sentences.en: And there's some very severe disadvantages to it.
sentences.zh: 并且也有一些非常严重的劣势。

sentences.en: And sometimes, you know, I have to fail 12 times when I could have just failed three times if I just asked somebody, you know, but I just don't.
sentences.zh: 有时候，你知道，我本可以如果直接问别人就只需失败三次，但我却不得不失败十二次，你知道的，但我就是不问。

sentences.en: I had a conversation with that, with my wife last night, um, about our daughter who's seven and she's, uh, and I was, I, she, we were telling her, you know,
sentences.zh: 我昨晚和我妻子谈过这件事，嗯，关于我们七岁的女儿，她，呃，然后我，她，我们在告诉她，你知道的，

sentences.en: you can just do things in this order and this is how it works.
sentences.zh: 你可以按这个顺序做事情，这就是它的运作方式。

sentences.en: And she was really trying to break the whole system and reinvent the wheel and find out a new way to do it and kind of getting in trouble.
sentences.zh: 而她真的在试图打破整个系统，重新发明轮子，并找出一种新的做事方法，结果惹上了一点麻烦。

sentences.en: And I was like, no, look, you can do it this way.
sentences.zh: 我当时就说，不，听着，你可以用这种方式做。

sentences.en: And this is what everyone's done.
sentences.zh: 这就是每个人都在做的。

sentences.en: You can do what you're doing, but you're probably going to be here for three hours doing this short that you don't want to do.
sentences.zh: 你可以按你现在的做法来，但你可能得在这里花上三个小时来做这个你根本不想做的短活。

sentences.en: So, and that's fine.
sentences.zh: 所以，这倒也没关系。

sentences.en: And, you know, Emily's like, what are you doing?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，艾米莉就问，你在干什么？

sentences.en: And I was like, I'm not telling her to go either way.
sentences.zh: 我当时就说，我没有告诉她该选哪条路。

sentences.en: Cause I see myself, but that left-hand path, I just wanted to know that this is a harder way to do it and, and really pick when you do that because, um, I'm an intuitive learner.
sentences.zh: 因为我看到了我自己，那条左手之路，我只是想知道这是一条更难走的路，当你要这样做时一定要认真选择，因为，嗯，我是个直觉型学习者。

sentences.en: I'm an experiential learner.
sentences.zh: 我是个体验型学习者。

sentences.en: When somebody tries to say, here's the way that it has to be done.
sentences.zh: 当有人试图说，事情就必须得这么做。

sentences.en: And I'm like, what if I skip step three and do eight?
sentences.zh: 而我会想，如果我跳过第三步直接做第八步会怎么样？

sentences.en: And what if I do?
sentences.zh: 如果我这么做会怎么样？

sentences.en: And I want to fail a lot of times, prove to myself and, but it's a harder way to be, but ultimately I think you'd learn more, you know, you'd discover stuff.
sentences.zh: 我想要失败很多次，向自己证明，而且，虽然这是一条更艰难的生存方式，但最终我认为你会学到更多，你知道的，你会发现一些东西。

sentences.en: But yeah, I mean, you know, there are pluses and minuses to everything that way.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，我的意思是，你知道，用那种方式看，任何事情都有利有弊。

sentences.en: And, and I, you know, circling back to the martial arts thing, one of the things that I feel like I learned the most from martial arts was how to learn how to do stuff.
sentences.zh: 而且，而且我，你知道，回到武术这件事上，我觉得我从武术中学到最多的事情之一，就是如何去学习做事情。

sentences.en: Um, a lot of the things that I learned to do early in my life, I learned frankly, in a half ass way, because I was such a cussed individualist about it, you know?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我早年学会做的很多事情，坦率地说，学得都半斤八两，因为我在这些事情上是个极其固执的个人主义者，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And, um, having somebody say, okay, this is the sequence of stuff you have to learn and you just have to do it this way and don't ask any questions, or at least, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，有个人对我说，好吧，这是你必须学习的步骤顺序，你必须照这样去做，而且不要问任何问题，或者至少，你知道的，

sentences.en: you can ask questions, but the answer is always going to be the same thing.
sentences.zh: 你可以问问题，但答案永远都是一样的。

sentences.en: You know, um, that actually has helped me learn other things subsequently a lot faster because I, I spend a little bit less time screwing around,
sentences.zh: 你知道，嗯，这实际上帮助我后来学其他东西快了很多，因为我花在瞎折腾上的时间少了一点，

sentences.en: whereas sort of my MO when I was a kid for learning something was kind of undirected.
sentences.zh: 然而我小时候学习某样东西的惯用方式有点漫无目的。

sentences.en: You know, it was sort of like, Hey, here's a bunch of stuff.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这有点像，嘿，这里有一堆东西。

sentences.en: Let me try and make this thing or do this thing.
sentences.zh: 让我试着造这个东西或者做这个东西。

sentences.en: But I didn't, I didn't, you know, have a real rigorous practiced, you know, sequential way of getting through something.
sentences.zh: 但我并没有，我并没有，你知道的，有一种真正严谨的、练习过的、循序渐进的方式来攻克某件事。

sentences.en: And, and actually a lot of times it's a lot faster to do it that way.
sentences.zh: 而且，事实上很多时候，用那种方式做会快得多。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, can you talk about the process of making a sword?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，你能谈谈制作一把剑的过程吗？

sentences.en: I mean, we did an episode on katanas and talked about it a little bit, but it's like, you know, you're clay tempering to bend these things.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们做过一期关于武士刀的节目并稍微讨论过，但就像，你知道的，你要用覆土淬火来弯曲这些东西。

sentences.en: Um, so traditionally the starting point is the steel.

sentences.en: And so steel in Japan was directly smelted, which not to be too nerdy about it was unusual in terms of the metallurgy of steel in, in, in iron in history.
sentences.zh: 因此日本的钢是直接冶炼出来的，如果别太书呆子气的话，这在历史上的钢和铁冶金学中是不寻常的。

sentences.en: Um, but basically, you know, you had a big bin of charcoal and iron ore and you set it on fire and you just burn it for a long time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但基本上，你知道的，你有一个大木炭箱和铁矿石，你把它点燃，然后烧很长时间。

sentences.en: And by doing it in a very, very precise way, what you end up with in the bottom is steel and looks like a moon rock.
sentences.zh: 通过一种非常非常精确的方式，你最后在底部得到的是钢，它看起来像一块月球岩石。

sentences.en: It doesn't look at all like anything you could make a sword out of.
sentences.zh: 它看起来一点也不像你能用来做剑的东西。

sentences.en: So, and so you have to then refine that.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以你必须对其进行精炼。

sentences.en: And so there were many, many different techniques in Japan, but they all basically involved taking, you know, busting up this chunk of steel, smashing it, layering it,
sentences.zh: 因此日本有非常非常多的技术，但它们基本上都包括，把这块钢砸碎，粉碎，分层，

sentences.en: and then heating it so hot that all those layers would stick together.
sentences.zh: 然后加热到很高的温度，让所有这些层粘合在一起。

sentences.en: So then you would draw that out, fold it over and do it again.
sentences.zh: 然后你把它拉长，对折，再做一次。

sentences.en: And you just had to do this over and over because there was so much crud in the steel and the carbon content was heterogeneous.

sentences.en: And there were all these different factors that made it necessary to repeat this many times.
sentences.zh: 还有所有这些不同的因素使得必须重复这个过程很多次。

sentences.en: And that process yielded a steel that was beautiful.
sentences.zh: 这个过程产生了一种美丽的钢。

sentences.en: It was just visually interesting, especially if you polish, you know, if you polish it in a certain way.
sentences.zh: 它在视觉上很有趣，特别是如果你抛光，你知道，如果你用某种特定方式抛光的话。

sentences.en: And so that's the most traditional starting point for a Japanese sword.
sentences.zh: 所以这是日本刀最传统的起点。

sentences.en: Now today we can go down to, you know, steel store and buy steel and just make it from there.
sentences.zh: 现在今天我们可以去，你知道，钢材店买钢材然后直接从那开始制作。

sentences.en: Oh, I, I mean, I completely would lose money if I did $7,000 for a sword, $20,000.

sentences.en: Um, and a lot of people think that this is the hard part and it's not easy.

sentences.en: You know, it's not a, it's not a lay down to forge it.

sentences.zh: 不，不，那是闪电。

sentences.en: But, um, you've ingered the, uh, gods, uh, apparently so, um, so, uh, anyway, um, you know, once, once you forge it, then you have to, um, actually grind it to shape.
sentences.zh: 但是，嗯，你惹恼了，呃，诸神，呃，显然是这样，嗯，所以，呃，不管怎样，嗯，你知道，一旦，一旦你锻造好它，然后你必须，嗯，实际把它研磨成形。

sentences.en: And, uh, traditionally they ground it by hand on brick shaped little, you know, abrasive stones.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，传统上他们是用砖块形状的小块，你知道的，研磨砂轮进行手工研磨的。

sentences.en: And that process also extremely, extremely slow.
sentences.zh: 而且这个过程也极其、极其缓慢。

sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我通常会做的是完成大部分的工作。

sentences.en: these traditional Japanese water stones, just ridiculously time consuming.
sentences.zh: 这些传统的日本水磨石上完成那些最后的阶段，简直是荒谬地耗时。

sentences.en: Um, so you, you're spending, you know, if you do it the most traditional way, you're spending all this time at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，你要花，你知道的，如果你用最传统的方式做，你在开始时就要花掉所有这些时间。

sentences.en: And then you're spending a lot of time at the end too.
sentences.zh: 然后你在最后也要花很多时间。

sentences.en: Anyway, once you've polished it to a particular shape, then it's time to heat treat it, to harden it up to this point.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，一旦你把它抛光成特定的形状，就是时候进行热处理了，在这一点上将其硬化。

sentences.en: To make sure that the spine is softer.

sentences.en: But, um, the term for what, what happens is you get something you can actually see it's a visual marker of this distinction between the hard edge and the soft spine.

sentences.en: And so the soft spine gives it the shock resistance and the hard edge gives it edge holding and, you know, ability to cut hard stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以柔软的刀脊赋予了它抗冲击性，而坚硬的刀刃赋予了它保持锋利度的能力，以及，你知道的，切割坚硬东西的能力。

sentences.en: So, um, you know, to, to accomplish that, you have to cover the spine with a clay that acts as sort of a heat sink or an insulator.

sentences.en: And then you heat the whole thing up to about 1500 degrees and you plunge it into water.

sentences.en: And in about three seconds, the edge will convert from a soft steel to a hard steel.

sentences.en: And so there's this little wavy line called a hemone that runs down the, uh, the blade.
sentences.zh: 所以有一条沿着，呃，刀身延伸的小波浪线，叫做刃文。

sentences.en: And you can tell a lot about where the sword was made and who it was made by and when it was made and all that sort of thing by how the hemone is shaped.

sentences.en: And as they get better at it in the record, you start, as they get better at the process, which it's amazing that they figured that.

sentences.en: It's like, they had no idea, you know, this was trial and error, which is pretty amazing, you know, to generationally pass down that knowledge.

sentences.zh: 艺术创作或者你的心路历程随着时间如何变化有什么看法吗？

sentences.zh: 在经历这种艺术发展、职业发展的过程中，你会去克服什么，或者弄清楚关于自己的什么事情吗？

sentences.en: I always tell people that I am the exact same person I was when I was 13 years old.
sentences.zh: 我总是告诉别人，我跟13岁时完全是同一个人。

sentences.zh: 我，而且，而且我，我真的在很大程度上相信这是真的。

sentences.en: I,
sentences.zh: 我，

sentences.zh: 我觉得我的人生并不是在深刻地改变我是谁，而是变得更加擅长让13岁的自己在世界上游刃有余。

sentences.en: So it's been more instrumental stuff, you know, but I was always just confident and happy in who I was.

sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，所以我，我只是，我，我从来不是一个在内心深处有过挣扎的人。

sentences.zh: 我总是对外界的事物感到挣扎，但我从没有真正和自己过不去。

sentences.en: And so, you know, what I've just tried to, to do is just be a little more effective and a little bit less, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我一直在尝试做的，就是让自己更有效率一点，少一点，你知道，

sentences.en: except the things that I suck at and, and, you know,
sentences.zh: 接受我不擅长的东西，而且，你知道，

sentences.zh: 但我不会试图去改变它们，因为我大多数不擅长的东西，并不是，你知道，那些会毁了我生活的滑铁卢。

sentences.en: So, yeah, you know, if you're one of my patients is listening, I swear I didn't set Walter up to say that, but a lot of them have,

sentences.en: it isn't really discovering or figuring out anything new.
sentences.zh: 这其实并不是去发现或弄懂什么新东西。

sentences.en: It's figuring out how to go back to who you always knew you were, but be less ashamed of that and more effective at that in the world.
sentences.zh: 这是在弄清楚如何回到你一直知道的那个自己，但对那个自己少一点羞耻感，在世界上更有效率地展现出来。

sentences.en: You know, it's dealing with the world's reaction to you, not really figuring out what you need to do.

sentences.en: But, you know, you also want to be careful with that because it's like, you know, talking about Joseph Campbell, as soon as you stop changing on that monomyth,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，你对此也要小心，因为这就像，你知道，聊到约瑟夫·坎贝尔，一旦你停止在那个单一神话中改变，

sentences.en: And so, you know, that force, I mean, if you're, if you always, I mean, I, you know, it's the sort of the shark.

sentences.en: I just, that's what I just swim in.
sentences.zh: 我只是，那就是我在其中畅游的东西。

sentences.zh: 那就是我的，那就是我的世界。

sentences.en: I'm not that interested in my problems or I'm not that interested in why I can or can't do this or what, you know, I just, I just try to focus on things out there and, and,
sentences.zh: 我对自己的问题没那么大兴趣，或者我对为什么我能或不能做这个、或者什么，你知道，我只是，我只是努力把注意力放在外面的事物上，然后，

sentences.zh: 听起来好像是，哦，对呀，站起来干就完了，老兄。

sentences.en: You know, it's harder than that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，实际没那么简单。

sentences.en: But, um, uh, but I, I, I, you know, I, everybody wants to generalize from, from, from their own psychology to what other people.
sentences.zh: 但是，嗯，但是，我，我，我，你知道，每个人都想从他们自己的心理出发，去推断其他人。

sentences.en: I'll be doing or thinking, you know, but I, I mean, I, I, I really, I, I really do, uh,

sentences.en: Hmm.

sentences.zh: 我是说，关于你的艺术本质，或者，嗯，你知道，你觉得未来会走向何方，还有什么别的吗？

sentences.en: Um, so one thing that people, uh, underestimate or, or don't look at with respect to art is, um, you know, we have this, um, uh, idea about art.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以人们对艺术有一个低估的、或者说，呃，不太看得清的方面，就是，嗯，我们对艺术有一种，呃，

sentences.zh: 我们当中许多人从这种浪漫主义时期延续下来的观念，即艺术全都是关于，你知道的，自我启示，就像在谈论拜伦勋爵以及那种，对，对，对。

sentences.zh: 当你在，当你，当你回到这一点上时，搞艺术就变得更容易了。

sentences.en: And, and again, it gets back to that, you know, martial arts thing of do the thing as sincerely as possible.

sentences.en: And it's like, you know, like we had to make houses, we had to make swords, we had to make pipes, we had to make chairs.

sentences.en: But then in doing that, we kind of had to make them be in conversation with a culture and we put little things into them that make me different.
sentences.zh: 但随后在做这些事情的过程中，我们不得不让它们与某种文化进行对话，我们在其中融入了一些让我与众不同的小细节。

sentences.en: We had to, we, people didn't have to make them beautiful.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不，人们其实并非必须把它们做得精美绝伦。

sentences.en: They just sort of want to do that.
sentences.zh: 他们只是有一种那样做的冲动。

sentences.en: And so it's like my work with a lot of creatives and that's what I always tell them is like, I don't know what kind of art I want to make.
sentences.zh: 所以，就像我跟很多创意工作者合作时那样，这也是我一直对他们说的：我不知道我想创作什么样的艺术。

sentences.en: I don't know, poem, whatever.

sentences.en: And I'm like, no, just go make a thing.

sentences.en: And then the art comes from that, you know, and the artists that I profile and write about, like, I love, I love the history of like lounge chairs specifically, right.

sentences.en: But the Eames and how they kind of are in conversation anticipating a future they don't even really live to see, you know,

sentences.en: And then the flow doesn't work.

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.en: And, and when you, but you're making a pipe, you're making a chair, you're making a sword, you're making a building.

sentences.en: You're in conversation with something that people need, what you start with, and then it sort of becomes you.

sentences.en: And that's always like the journey that I'm tracking when I biography artists on our, on our podcast or on our blog.

sentences.en: And, you know, to me, one of the great things about, you know, any kind of craft, physical craft, is that the materials are the materials.

sentences.en: And that, that discovery, I mean, you know, one of the, the things that, that people kind of fetishize in, you know, in our cultures, you know,

sentences.en: the transcendent genius who figured out how to do this or that.

sentences.en: And so often I think geniuses are people who were just really attentive to something, you know, a material or a process or,

sentences.en: or a requirement that other people had just kind of said, oh, that's never, we can't, we can't get over that or whatever.
